decisions.rationale: All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor concerns the remote editor transport retry and its user-visible failure oracle. Host-aware projections, remote cache trust, and terminal attach recovery are plausible neighbors, but each has a different state owner or recovery lifecycle.

All 145 comparators were considered. Thread-worktree binding and lifecycle covers the same handoff identity, frozen context, stale binding, reconciliation, and recovery lifecycle. Identity storage, validation, file pivots, and background routing are narrower consumers or data-model seams.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is a governance gate for promoting file/editor packet fields into owner and wiring rows. The nearby owner-split, command-wiring, namespace, and worktree-catalog features govern adjacent artifacts but not this packet-promotion lifecycle.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is bridged-provider launch admission for a frozen cwd, including canonicalization and TOCTOU behavior. Worktree identity, validation, file pivots, merge-tool cwd scoping, background routing, and tombstones are related but have distinct consumers and transition owners.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is a restart owner map separating several operational domains. The nearby entries cover individual owner splits, panels, command workflows, or package lanes, so none represents the same multi-domain governance feature.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is transactional recovery for ledger-to-Plans lossless conversion. Plans-to-code handoff validation and remote-cache atomic publication have analogous transaction concerns but different authorities, artifacts, and lifecycles.

All 145 comparators were considered. This contract couples terminal packet buildability with one bounded SSH retry under GitHub Integration. Terminal session recovery and host-aware projection recovery are adjacent, but neither has the same combined authority and terminal packet lifecycle.

All 145 comparators were considered. Worktree lifecycle and branch identity is the same WorktreeManager-owned creation identity feature, including path-derived identity and collision concerns. Lane allocation, startup validity, chat auto-create races, and storage tombstones remain distinct lifecycle or consumer seams.

All 145 comparators were considered. The only plausible Unraid neighbor models result-enum transitions. The anchor instead governs XML round-trip preservation and merge conflicts, with a different artifact lifecycle and failure contract.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor deliberately combines removal and merge safety across command registration and executor semantics. The nearby features split confirmation, thread lifecycle, destructive cleanup, merge safety, delete UI, irreversibility, and pre-merge guards into distinct authorities or narrower lifecycles; none is the same combined feature.

All 145 comparators were considered. Resend truncates conversational history as part of message replay. Revert, rewind, and empty-revert behavior are plausible destructive-history neighbors, but they expose different commands, targets, and user-visible promises.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is the receipt completeness of a safe-point.restored event after exact-context verification. Completion receipts, rollback context, and file-mutation receipts are related evidence models but have different schemas, consumers, and lifecycle points.

All 145 comparators were considered. This feature is the package-aware runtime projection and pre-artifact handoff stack. Visible run-to-repo lineage, DAG package-lane scheduling, and plans-to-code handoff are adjacent but owned by different projection, scheduling, or compile lifecycles.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is the GitHub Actions integration identity boundary and degraded-state behavior. Command coverage, namespace migration, pin persistence, and consolidated panel ownership are separate subfeatures and do not cover the same integration lifecycle.

All 145 comparators were considered. Thread-worktree binding and lifecycle represents the same runtime worktree identity, survival, cleanup, reconciliation, deletion, and recovery feature. Lineage gates, destructive cleanup, conflict persistence, allocation, and validity are related but separately governed slices.

All 145 comparators were considered. Operational coverage and Source Control workflows is the same Source Control command-and-navigation product family under the Source Control authority. Compare, conflict, commit, graph, remote review, hunk, merge, ownership-boundary, and panel features are related specialized lifecycles.

All 145 comparators were considered. Worktree command catalog and production wiring matches the same canonical UI command family, compatibility normalization, handlers, selectors, disabled reasons, receipts, accessibility, and tests. Confirmation, authority splits, lifecycle races, destructive recovery, and branch identity remain separate contracts.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is the explicit Source Control-versus-Orchestrator context allocation in DL-011. Worktree owner splits, Source Control surface ownership, operational panels, and package lanes are neighboring owner decisions but not the same two-owner context contract.

All 145 comparators were considered. The stable-owner command group includes the canonical runtime recovery mapping and exact worktree baseline validation required to turn this Source Control CTA into an executable route, so it represents the same recovery-action feature. Terminal recovery and panel-wide recovery ownership remain distinct.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is account, repository, and environment binding plus the auth-refresh transition lifecycle for GitHub Actions. Operational commands, namespace aliases, foundational auth wiring, and pin state are adjacent but have different state machines or consumers.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is contradiction evidence that preserves owner boundaries without promoting packaging prose. Owner splits, project/thread command authority, namespace reservations, and Source Control surface ownership are related governance decisions, not the same evidence-retention feature.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is closure of the executor classified-outcome matrix over mandatory blocked codes. Terminal reason refinements, budget mappings, deferred terminality, and runtime recovery routes are adjacent taxonomies with different authorities and transition contracts.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is a canonical field-name contradiction within the safe-point model. Completion-receipt rollback fields and source-control safety vocabulary are neighboring schema concerns, but neither is the same alias and migration decision.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is generic event identity and deduplication semantics. Terminal events, worktree events, merge/PR schemas, test seglog, operation-card transitions, and degraded ingestion each use separate event families and consumers.

All 145 comparators were considered. Background worktree-context routing safety states the same fail-open defect: absent worktree context silently becomes main-project context. Thread binding, identity authority, validation, storage, frozen pivots, mode invariance, mutation receipts, and tombstones are distinct supporting seams.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor constrains route authority to run, object, and worktree identity rather than filter noise. Operational route persistence, stable-owner navigation, and visible run-to-repo pivots are related consumers but do not share the exact projection contract.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is a cross-surface accessibility and localization contract for operational projections, routing, queues, errors, and destructive controls. Allocation UI, filter state, thread icons, file-manager root projection, and review heat maps are narrower surfaces with distinct promises.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor requires immutable capture of dirty safe-point content. Completion receipts, source-control rollback context, and file-mutation receipt identity are related evidence contracts but do not own snapshot creation and restoration.

All 145 comparators were considered. This feature defines global stop precedence for FileSafe bypass, uncertain side effects, and untrusted projections. Destructive Source Control execution, runtime recovery mapping, merge safety, and rollback policy are nearby but have narrower authorities.

All 145 comparators were considered. Worktree-aware file identity is the same promise that file pivots and historical evidence remain bound to exact repo, worktree, and relative-path identity rather than silently substituting variants. Review identity, root projection, LSP roots, and tombstones are related consumers.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor governs external drag/drop direction, eligible destinations, and deterministic multi-item ordering. Clipboard/paste/save-copy and file creation/deletion are adjacent file mutations but use different input channels and lifecycle contracts.

All 145 comparators were considered. Host-aware search, editor, and LSP projections has the same remote recovery promise that stale or local-only recovered state cannot regain write authority without reconnect and revalidation. Terminal attach recovery and remote cache trust are distinct.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is an explicit multi-owner boundary among FileManager, Search, LSP, FileSafe, and Source Control. Search tool separation, LSP mutations, Source Control surface ownership, LSP roots, and host projections are individual owner features, not the same combined map.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is the canonical local file/editor vocabulary and owner note. GUI shell composition and cross-surface identity lifecycle consume nearby terms but do not own this vocabulary contract.

All 145 comparators were considered. Source-control compare and review identity safety is the same exact-target, no-silent-substitution feature as cross-worktree compare identity. Graph/history navigation, remote review, file pivots, and accessible review state are adjacent consumers.

All 145 comparators were considered. The defect is missing dependency and unblock metadata in FileManager PlanUnits despite documented prerequisites. Parallel admission, dependency worktree execution, and plans-to-code handoff are related compile consumers but not the same PlanUnit dependency contract.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is the editor buffer save-state taxonomy and its failure-preserves-dirty behavior. Save-copy and create/delete mutations are related file operations but have different identities, commands, and recovery promises.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is the FileManager offline-mode label and prohibition on pretend-live remote capabilities. Terminal recovery, advisory fetch, remote cache trust, and host-aware projections are related but governed by different surfaces and state machines.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor requires a normative action-derivation matrix from mutation guard inputs. Destructive Source Control semantics, runtime recovery routing, and authority-to-mutation policy are related decision systems with distinct owners and outputs.

All 145 comparators were considered. Git conflict and destructive diff transitions covers the same diff-side destructive action, safe-point, propagation, rollback, and undo lifecycle. Hunk index mutations, multi-file revert/rewind, empty revert, and operation cards remain distinct commands or projections.

All 145 comparators were considered. Open With is a target capability-negotiation and trust-validation feature. Foundational file commands, clipboard/save-copy, and create/delete are nearby file actions but have different command outcomes and authorization boundaries.

All 145 comparators were considered. Search and replace command workflow is the same preserved-snapshot, stale-result rejection, bulk-write safety, partial-failure, cancellation, and postcondition lifecycle. LSP mutations, revert transactions, and generic mutation receipts are related but distinct.

All 145 comparators were considered. File clipboard, paste, and save-copy operations covers the same pending copy/cut record, invalidation, destination validation, partial failure, rollback, and projection refresh lifecycle. File creation/deletion is a neighboring mutation family.

All 145 comparators were considered. This anchor is the FileManager-to-Source-Control handoff contract with canonical commands, exact revision identity, guards, refresh, and conformance evidence. Source Control workflows, generic wiring, runtime routing, review identity, and surface ownership remain separate producer or consumer contracts.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor governs accessibility and localization of transient UI categories across FileManager. Worktree allocation status, filters, icons, root projections, and review heat maps are plausible but narrower user-visible surfaces.

All 145 comparators were considered. Mention lookup and opening is an authorization-filtered, rename/delete-aware reference lifecycle. Worktree identity authority, file pivots, and repository tombstones are adjacent identity models with different consumers and security promises.

All 145 comparators were considered. File clipboard, paste, and save-copy operations explicitly includes Save Local Copy as the same durable copy-out mutation with destination validation, partial-failure recovery, and projection refresh. Create/delete and generic mutation receipts are related.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is compatibility-only lineage for a retired FileManager bridge with a no-work-node boundary. Worktree UI exclusions, backend exclusions, and shell composition are neighboring negative constraints but not the same retired artifact.

All 145 comparators were considered. LSP mutators lacking result and recovery semantics is the same semantic-mutation apply feature: capability checks, stale edit rejection, approval, multi-file completion, failure, and recovery. Search mutation and generic mutation receipts are distinct callers.

All 145 comparators were considered. Workspace, window, browser, terminal, branch, and command-block identity lifecycle represents the same missing lifecycle synchronization for separate browser and terminal tab identities. Terminal reveal races, PTY identity boundaries, and terminal recovery are narrower.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is a FileManager file/artifact error classification-to-recovery contract. Runtime route mapping, file mutations, terminal recovery, and host projections are related recovery systems with different authorities and state machines.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor covers the canonical file-tree action family plus guards, confirmations, disabled reasons, failure outcomes, and keyboard behavior. Foundational wiring and concrete mutation families are related, but their grouped authorities and lifecycles do not equal this whole tree-action contract.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is composition and transition semantics for environment, degradation, and preview-trust tokens. Ambient discovery trust, remote cache trust, and host projection freshness are consumers with distinct security and recovery boundaries.

All 145 comparators were considered. Git hunk stage and unstage index mutations is the same hunk action catalog requiring authoritative commands, payloads, preconditions, propagation, race handling, and recovery. Conflict and destructive diff transitions are a related but distinct lifecycle.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is Go-to-symbol provider merge, dedupe, freshness, cancellation, and invalid-location behavior. Search tool separation, LSP mutation, LSP root identity, and host-aware projections are neighboring provider or projection contracts.

All 145 comparators were considered. Breadcrumb and outline fallback is a user-visible LSP-to-heuristic freshness and accessibility lifecycle. Search separation, file-manager root projection, LSP root identity, and host projections are related but not the same fallback promise.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is path realization hardening for identity-based file open, including containment, symlink, TOCTOU, and active-worktree revision checks. Worktree authority, file pivots, remote-cache path trust, and tombstones are adjacent identity layers.

All 145 comparators were considered. Host-aware Search, Source-Control, and LSP projections represents the same consumer projection lifecycle for freshness, versioning, remote recovery, and non-stale authority. Search tool boundaries, generic routing, and LSP root keys are distinct support contracts.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is delivery, ordering, idempotency, dirty-buffer conflict, and refresh behavior for confirmed restore events. Diff transitions, revert/rewind, empty revert, operation cards, and completion receipts are separate operation or projection lifecycles.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is editor persistence schema, migration, transaction, corruption, concurrency, retention, and restore. Thread-binding storage, cross-surface identity lifecycle, and host projections persist related state but have different record owners.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is secure lifecycle and partial restore for browser, terminal, and other workspace adjunct sessions. Workspace close orchestration, terminal sessions, dev-session evidence, and identity lifecycle are related but differ in scope, owners, or retained data.

All 145 comparators were considered. This feature is the taxonomy, precedence, transitions, and accessible projection of Git state versus restore feedback. Review identity, conflict transitions, graph navigation, and heat-map state are neighboring Source Control projections with different promises.

All 145 comparators were considered. Large-file editor thresholds and Load full file transitions are owned by FileManager. Terminal performance and terminal protocol fixtures share scale concerns but operate under a different renderer, workload, and failure lifecycle.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is an entrypoint-to-command conformance map for delegating UI search actions. Search-tool separation, search/replace workflow, and stable-owner routing are related but have different consumers or command lifecycles.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor is Search-index build cancellation, partial-generation removal, and mandatory fresh rebuild after re-enable. Search tool boundaries, crash-atomic cache publication, and host projection recovery are adjacent but distinct lifecycle owners.

All 145 comparators were considered. After all 145 comparisons, no comparator addressed the exact live-owner disposition that restores FileManager sections 10 through 12 and retires the missing-section placeholder.

All 145 comparators were considered. Ambient Discovery is the same discovery/type-ahead product pipeline whose trust, hidden-path, watcher, cache, and data boundaries govern these results. Search tooling, remote cache, and host projections remain distinct providers or storage layers.

All 145 comparators were considered. This is general file transfer progress, collision, checksum, atomic commit, retry/resume, offline recovery, and cleanup. Clipboard/save-copy, Docker publish delivery, and remote cache trust are analogous but different transfer products.

All 145 comparators were considered. Editor shortcut routing and floating-window focus arbitration have no same-feature comparator. Terminal input and IME handling is the only plausible keyboard neighbor, but it has a different surface, authority, and interaction state machine.

All 145 comparators were considered. The anchor intentionally preserves sparse implementation seams across editor, preview, browser, and chat. Shell composition, cross-panel lineage, and identity lifecycle are related cross-surface contracts but do not define the same seam handoffs.

All 145 comparators were considered. File revert, rewind, and destructive-action safety represents the same exact-target revert operation requiring base revision, preconditions, revalidation, stale rejection, outcome evidence, refresh, and recovery. Review identity, diff transitions, hunk mutations, and empty revert are distinct.
